notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Jeremiah 18, because I wasn't able to read a single source page.

The research tool stopped me at my first attempt. I'd set it to open the verse-by-verse pages for this chapter on enduringword.com, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, preceptaustin.org and netbible.org. Each time it said I had no tool calls left for this turn, and no page content came through. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have nothing from the pages, I've left everything out rather than make up notes or links.

When the tool is working again, I'll:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** read the pages listed above and write a note for each verse with its link.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** the main question is likely vv. 6–10, about the potter and his clay and whether God "relents." I'd look at what Reformed teachers say (ligonier.org, monergism.com, thegospelcoalition.org) against Wesleyan and Methodist ones (wesley.nnu.edu, seedbed.com). The question of how to read Jeremiah's prayer against his enemies in vv. 19–23 could go to gty.org and desiringgod.org.
3. **Other views:** the netbible.org notes and bibleodyssey.org for modern scholarship; newadvent.org, catholic.com and oca.org for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'd include a popular modern teaching only if one of the allowed sites actually discusses it in connection with this chapter.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start the research from scratch.
